subject.title: Feature: Session fork, resume, and continue (like open-agent-sdk)

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic public session lifecycle contract now, and should the first supported surface be SDK/Gateway APIs, CLI/chat commands, or a narrower Codex/native-thread subset?
rationale: Current main has partial primitives in several owners, but the public fork/resume/continue semantics require maintainer choices about identity, lineage, permissions, provider state, and upgrade-safe UX before implementation.

options.title: Design Unified Lifecycle Contract
options.body: Create a maintainer-owned design for generic fork, resume-by-ID, and continue-latest semantics across SDK, Gateway, CLI/chat/TUI, provider state, and docs before implementation.

options.title: Land Narrow Resume First
options.body: Treat chat or CLI resume-by-ID as a staged subset while keeping fork and continue-latest tracked under this broader contract.

options.title: Keep Codex Subset Separate
options.body: Document that Codex native-thread tools solve only Codex user-home workflows and defer generic OpenClaw session lifecycle APIs.

recommendation.title: Design Unified Lifecycle Contract
recommendation.body: Create a maintainer-owned design for generic fork, resume-by-ID, and continue-latest semantics across SDK, Gateway, CLI/chat/TUI, provider state, and docs before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to both the SDK package introduction and the recent Codex native-thread subset, making him the best available owner for the cross-surface product/API decision.
